1.why: All eight screens are static cards with no animations, carousels, or pop-up dialogs, only a fixed header, one card, and a logs panel.

2.why: Bold dark headings and a single high-contrast blue primary button dominate each step, though the large dark 'Logs' block competes visually and step 1 has two grey notice boxes.

3.why: Each screen presents one labelled field and one action button, so the next task is easy to locate, but step 1 buries the email field under three paragraphs of privacy/simulation text.

4.why: She must carry a 40-character recovery token and the MFA code 246810 from the Logs panel into input fields, remember 12-character password composition rules, and track a 7-step flow with no progress indicator.

5.why: No password manager hint, autofill affordance, 'remember me' checkbox, or show-password toggle appears on any screen.

6.why: Only the recovery token is pre-filled in step 3; there are no saved emails, remembered devices, or recognisable saved items anywhere else in the flow.

7.why: Sentences are short and legible, but step 1 uses technical/jargon phrasing such as 'browser-only simulation', 'account-bound recovery token', and 'privacy-neutral test recovery token'.

8.why: No error or validation state is shown in any of the eight screenshots, so no message describing a problem and its fix is present.

9.why: Fields have no placeholder examples or sample formats; the password rule is stated in prose ('at least 12 characters...') but no example password or email format is shown.

10.why: The password and one-time code steps are clearly labelled ('New password', 'Verification code'), but no alternative sign-in options such as biometric/face login are offered or explained.

11.why: Every screen offers exactly one input and one primary button, with no competing menus or branching options.

12.why: Each action yields a clear outcome message ('recovery instructions will be sent securely', 'Your medication review appointment request has been confirmed') plus cumulative log entries, though the step-1 result message is deliberately ambiguous.

13.why: Each step has one short instructional line and the password rule is stated, but there are no help links, tooltips, or guidance on where to find the token/MFA code.

14.why: No back link, cancel, 'resend code', or 'start over' control appears on any screen, so recovering from a mistyped token or code is not supported in the visible UI.

15.why: All screens reuse the same header, white rounded card, field styling, blue button, logs panel, and safety footer, giving a highly consistent layout.
